docs.title: ETHRC Drone Racing
docs.text: Welcome to the ETHRC Drone Racing project documentation.

docs.title: Quick Links
docs.text:
• Getting Started: Set up your environment and run your first simulation.
  • Guidelines: Learn about our documentation standards and development workflow.

docs.title: Project Layout
docs.text:
The project is organized as follows:

  • docker/: Contains the Docker configuration, including the Dockerfile used to build the development and simulation environment.
  • px4/: Contains the PX4 Autopilot source code. This is where the flight control logic resides.
  • docs/: The source for this documentation site.
    • docs/: Markdown content files.
    • mkdocs.yml: Configuration for the MkDocs site generator.
  • docker-compose.yaml: Defines the services and volumes for running the simulation environment.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Check out the README.md in the root of the repository for instructions on how to build and run the simulation.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you set up the ETHRC Drone Racing environment using Docker.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Host OS: Ubuntu/Linux recommended.
  • Software: Docker Engine + Docker Compose v2 in Rootless mode. (Installation guide)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Note

After step 3, the container will be running in the background. You can stop it with docker compose down.

docs.title: Step 0: Set up SSH for GitHub
docs.text: We need SSH so git clone works smoothly without typing passwords. If you haven't done this, follow GitHub's guide.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the repository with submodules to include PX4:

git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:ETHRoboticsClub/ETHRC-Drone-Racing.git
cd ETHRC-Drone-Racing

docs.title: Step 3: Start Services
docs.text:
Enable GUI access, start the container, and open a shell:

# Allow container GUI apps to open windows on your desktop (X11)
xhost +local:root

# Start the container (detached) and open a shell inside
docker compose up -d
docker exec -it erc-aeronautics bash

docs.title: Step 4: Run Simulation
docs.text:
Inside the container, run the default simulation:

# Default x500 in the default world
cd /ws/px4/PX4-Autopilot
make px4_sitl gz_x500

docs.title: Project Guidelines
docs.text: This document outlines the guidelines for contributing to the ETHRC Drone Racing project, including documentation standards and development workflow.

docs.title: Documentation Guidelines
docs.text: We use MkDocs with the Material for MkDocs theme.

docs.title: Editing Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation source files are located in docs/docs/. They are written in Markdown.

  • Headers: Use # for page titles and ## for section headers.
  • Code Blocks: Use triple backticks (```) for code blocks. Specify the language for syntax highlighting (e.g., ```bash).
  • Images: Place images in docs/docs/images/ and reference them as ![Alt Text](images/filename.png).
  • Admonitions: Use admonitions for notes, warnings, and tips: 
    !!! note
    This is a note.

docs.title: Running Locally
docs.text:
To preview your changes locally, run the following command from the docs/ directory (or root if using the Docker container):

mkdocs serve

The site will be available at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Git Workflow
docs.text:
We follow a standard feature-branch workflow:

  1. Create a Branch: Create a new branch for your feature or fix. 
    git checkout -b feature/my-new-feature
  2. Commit Changes: Make your changes and commit them with clear, descriptive messages. 
    git commit -m "Add new flight controller logic"
  3. Push and PR: Push your branch to GitHub and open a Pull Request (PR) against main.
  4. Review and Merge: After review, merge the PR. Delete the branch after merging.

docs.title: Docker Environment
docs.text:
The project relies heavily on Docker to ensure a consistent environment.

  • Rebuilding: If you modify docker/Dockerfile or requirements.txt (if applicable), rebuild the image: 
    docker compose build
  • Running: Start the environment with: 
    docker compose up -d
